_comment: CSV cell-serialisation test vectors for hexa.core.csv.stringify_cell (asserted by hexa.core.tests.test_csv). `vectors` pins how a single cell serialises (post-guard, post-quote); `rowVectors` pins whole-record shape (columns + rows -> full CSV, no BOM), which cell vectors cannot cover because each is wrapped in a fixed two-column row. JSON-representable inputs only; type-specific branches (bytes/Decimal/datetime, plus non-finite and signed-zero floats) are covered directly in test_csv.py. Float expectations follow Python's str(), which is the shortest round-tripping form and matches the text Postgres itself prints for a float8 (e.g. 1e+16, 1e-07). Large integers are given as JSON strings to keep the fixture safe; they exercise the text/formula-guard branch, not number formatting.

vectors.description: null becomes an empty cell
boolean true is lowercased
boolean false is lowercased
plain text passes through
ordinary text that merely looks number-ish is not guarded
integer number
negative integer number is not an injection risk
decimal number
large float uses exponent notation, matching Postgres float8 text
fractional large float keeps its significant digits in exponent form
small float uses exponent notation with a zero-padded exponent
small float below the expand threshold stays in exponent form
large float above 1e21 uses exponent notation
numeric string preserved (negative decimal)
numeric string preserved (exponent)
numeric string preserved (leading dot)
big numeric string left intact (numeric literal, not formula-guarded)
formula = is guarded
formula + is guarded
formula @ is guarded
leading - on non-numeric text is guarded
number-looking but non-numeric leading - is guarded
value with a comma is quoted
embedded double quotes are doubled and quoted
embedded newline is quoted
guarded and quoted together (leading - plus comma)
object serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
array serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
non-ASCII text passes through literally (no \uXXXX escaping)
object with non-ASCII text stays literal in JSON (ensure_ascii=False), then quoted

rowVectors.description: header then one CRLF-terminated line per row
a lone empty field is written as "" (not a bare line), as Python's csv.writer does
a lone non-empty field is not quoted
single column mixes quoted-empty and plain rows
an all-empty multi-column row is a bare separator, never quoted
